LESSON: WRITING 11.5.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING – SPELLING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.5: Writing 11.5.1 Mechanics of Writing – Spelling
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 11.5.1 Mechanics of Writing – Spelling, part of Strand 11 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should you consider splitting words at the end of a line? 2. How do we abbreviate different words?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 11.5.1 Mechanics of Writing – Spelling together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: skill of learning independently when the learner writes abbreviations correctly.

• Collaboration: teamwork skill when the learner interacts with peers to undertake different activities in groups.

Values:
● Unity: the learner collaborates in pairs and groups to present rules on abbreviation and splitting of words.

● Responsibility: the learners write passages on how to make savings from income generating activities.

Link to other subjects:

The learner is able to relate the concept of writing abbreviations to their learning in Social Studies, Science and Technology and

Agriculture and Nutrition.
